abstract: This study demonstrates that animal-free 3D culture and long-term hypoxic conditioning modulate mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicle (MSC-EV) production and cargo composition without compromising MSC identity. Mimicking the in vivo microenvironment through hypoxic 3D culture increased MSC-EV yield and altered EV molecular composition, highlighting the potential of culture engineering as a strategy to optimise MSC-EV manufacturing. While 3D culture exerted the greatest effect on both cellular and MSC-EV proteomes, increasing protein abundance and complexity associated with translational and peptide biosynthesis pathways, hypoxic conditioning further enhanced the functional activity of 3D-derived MSC-EVs in an in vitro wound-healing model. These findings suggest that even subtle alterations in MSC-EV cargo can influence biological activity. Collectively, our results demonstrate that culture configuration and oxygen tension are important process variables that affect MSC-EV yield, composition, and functionality. This work highlights the importance of integrating physiologically relevant culture conditions into MSC-EV production strategies and provides insights for the development of scalable and clinically translatable MSC-EV therapeutics for wound healing and regenerative medicine.
